name: Akihabara core: 3 hours
tag: Retro games, old manga and toys, close to the station
why: For the first day after the flight. Three stops, short walks, and a place to sit on the top floor of Super Potato. It is built around the 1990s shonen and game shelves, which suits Dragon Ball Z, Digimon, Cowboy Bebop, Mario and Zelda.
steps: Akihabara Station, Electric Town exit
We meet here. Radio Kaikan is across the street, so there is almost no walking to start. If you are tired, tell me and we slow down.
Akihabara Radio Kaikan
Ten floors facing the station. We take the lift to the top and walk down. Figures and toys are on 3F to 7F, and K-BOOKS is on 3F.
Super Potato Akihabara

Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors, plus handhelds and Sega. The early Mario and Zelda games are on the Famicom and Super Famicom shelves. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade with a place to sit.
Mandarake Complex Akihabara
Boys' manga and vintage books on 3F. Toys on 6F to 8F, with Chogokin on 7F and robots on 8F. Stock changes every week, so we see what is there that day. We finish here at 13:00.
moves: All on foot, about ten minutes at most between shops. Radio Kaikan is across the street from the station, and Mandarake is about four minutes from the Electric Town exit.
good: A slow first day: a few shops, one tall building of toys, and somewhere to sit.
mind: Check that a Japanese game runs on your console at home, and on 100 V power, before you buy. A Famicom cartridge does not fit an NES without an adapter.

name: Akihabara deep: 5 hours
tag: Gunpla and model shops, retro games, lunch and Mandarake
why: For the most of Akihabara in one day. It keeps everything in course A and adds the Gunpla and model shops, a sit-down lunch and a longer stay at Mandarake. Good if Gundam Wing is high on the list.
steps: Akihabara Station, Electric Town exit
We meet here. Yodobashi is one minute away, so the first shop is almost at the door.
Yodobashi Akiba
Plastic models, modelling tools, figures and games are all on the 6th floor. A good first look at the current Gunpla kits.
Akihabara Radio Kaikan
Ten floors facing the station. Kaiyodo is on 5F, Yellow Submarine with its model kits on 6F, and Volks on 8F. We take the lift to the top and walk down.
Super Potato Akihabara
Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors, plus handhelds and Sega. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade with a place to sit.
Kotobukiya Akihabara-kan
The figure and model kit maker's own shop. It sells new releases and shop-only items, and the pop-ups change, so we see what is on that week.
Lunch at Go!Go!Curry

Kanazawa curry: a pork cutlet on a dark, thick roux, eaten at the counter. It is quick and close to the station. If you would rather sit down for a steak, Juke Steak serves lunch and I can swap it in.
Mandarake Complex Akihabara
Boys' manga and vintage books on 3F. Toys on 6F to 8F, with Chogokin on 7F and robots on 8F. Stock changes every week, so we see what is there that day.
Volks Hobby Tengoku 2
Seven floors of kits, figures and goods. Volks's own kits are on 4F, and the 6th and 7th floors host pop-up events that change. We finish here around 15:00.
moves: All on foot. Most legs are short, and the longest is from lunch to Mandarake. We work from the station south to Kotobukiya, then north.
good: Gunpla and figure fans who want the whole district in one day, with a proper lunch in the middle.
mind: Go!Go!Curry takes cash only, so bring some for the smaller shops too. The Dragon Ball Store is not in Akihabara: it is on the 1st floor of Tokyo Station Ichibangai, two stops away, and I can add it if you want it.

name: Akihabara and Shibuya: full day
tag: Akihabara in the morning, Nintendo and Pokémon in the afternoon
why: For both worlds. The morning is the short version of course A, and the afternoon is Shibuya for Mario, Zelda and Pokémon, with Nintendo TOKYO and the Pokémon Center on one floor.
steps: Akihabara Station, Electric Town exit
We meet here. Radio Kaikan is across the street.
Akihabara Radio Kaikan
Ten floors facing the station. We take the lift to the top and walk down. Figures and toys are on 3F to 7F.
Super Potato Akihabara
Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors. The early Mario and Zelda games are on the Famicom and Super Famicom shelves. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade.
Lunch at Go!Go!Curry
Kanazawa curry at the counter, quick and close to the station. An early lunch, so we are not hunting for food in Shibuya.
Train from Akihabara to Shibuya
About 30 to 40 minutes by train. I ride with you and tell you which line to take.
Nintendo TOKYO

Nintendo's own store on the 6th floor of Shibuya PARCO, five minutes on foot from Shibuya Station. On busy days entry is by numbered ticket, and a weekday is calmer. I check the store's page that morning.
Pokémon Center Shibuya
The official Pokémon store, on the same floor. Thirty to forty-five minutes is enough for most people.
Jump Shop Shibuya
Official Weekly Shonen Jump goods, also on the 6th floor. Dragon Ball is one of the series the Jump Shops cover, and what is in stock changes.
Mandarake Shibuya
One basement floor in the Shibuya BEAM building, five minutes from the Hachikō exit. Shonen comics, vintage comics and toys. We finish here around 17:00.
moves: Akihabara on foot in the morning, then one train ride of about 30 to 40 minutes. In Shibuya the three PARCO stores share one floor, and Mandarake is a five-minute walk away.
good: Nintendo and Pokémon fans who also want the Akihabara shelves, and do not mind one train ride.
mind: Shibuya PARCO has irregular closing days, so I check its calendar the week before. New Pokémon card products are sold by advance lottery, so sealed packs are unlikely, but the store is worth it for everything else. A Gundam Base is announced for the 5th floor of the same building from November 2026, and I will check whether it has opened.
